mainTopic: משכון of חמץ and 'מעכשיו', חמץ found after פסח, חמץ buried under rubble, and eating תרומה of חמץ on פסח
overview: The גמרא explains the ברייתא about a ישראל who holds a גוי's חמץ as a משכון. The תנא קמא and רבי מאיר argue about רבי יצחק's rule that a בעל חוב owns the משכון he holds. All agree that a גוי lender does not acquire a ישראל's משכון this way. The משנה still permits such חמץ after פסח, and the גמרא explains that this is a case where the גוי said 'מעכשיו'. A ברייתא about פת פורני proves that 'מעכשיו' makes a difference. A ברייתא then teaches that חמץ found in a store after פסח follows the owner of the store and its stock, not the workers. A new משנה says חמץ buried under rubble counts as destroyed, as long as it is beyond a dog's search (three טפחים), and רב חסדא adds that one must still do ביטול. Money buried by a שומר needs only one טפח, because it only has to be hidden from sight. Finally, a new משנה discusses eating תרומה of חמץ on פסח, and the גמרא begins by quoting a related משנה from מסכת תרומות.

steps.title: A new setup: the collateral was placed with the lender
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא sets up a new explanation of the ברייתא. The חמץ was deposited with the lender, and the תנאים argue about רבי יצחק's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what case are we dealing with? A case where the borrower placed the חמץ in the lender's hands. The two opinions disagree about the teaching of רבי יצחק.
steps.whatsHappening: The earlier explanation of the ברייתא did not work, so the גמרא offers a new one. This line is only a setup: it says what the argument is about, and the next lines explain it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא, a ישראל lent money to a גוי and took the גוי's חמץ as a משכון. The תנא קמא says the ישראל does not transgress, while רבי מאיר says he does. The new explanation is that the חמץ was physically with the ישראל lender, so the real question is whether holding a משכון makes the lender its owner.

keyTerms.meaning: 'With what are we dealing here?' The גמרא is about to set up a specific case.
He gave it as a pledge or collateral.

phrases.english: Rather, with what are we dealing here?
Such as where he (the gentile borrower) deposited it as collateral with him (the Jewish lender),
and they disagree regarding the teaching of Rabbi Yitzchak.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the earlier, rejected explanation of the ברייתא (on the previous עמוד).
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the case (אוקימתא) and moves the argument onto רבי יצחק's principle.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The earlier explanation of the ברייתא's argument did not hold up.
steps.terutzMaskana: The חמץ was deposited with the ישראל lender, and the argument is whether he owns it under רבי יצחק's rule.

steps.title: רבי יצחק: a creditor owns the collateral he holds
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק learns from 'ולך תהיה צדקה' that a בעל חוב acquires the משכון.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said: How do we know that a lender owns the collateral he holds? The פסוק says that returning the pledge 'will be a righteousness for you.' If the lender did not own it, what righteousness would there be in giving it back? So we learn that a lender owns the collateral.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רבי יצחק's teaching, which is the basis for the argument just mentioned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה praises a lender who returns a poor man's pledge at night and calls it צדקה. That praise only makes sense if the lender is giving up something that belongs to him. Therefore, while the lender holds the משכון, it counts as his property.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule is the key to the whole sugya. If the lender owns the משכון, then a ישראל holding חמץ as a משכון may be its owner on פסח.

phrases.english: As Rabbi Yitzchak said:
From where do we know that a creditor acquires the collateral?
As it is stated: 'And it shall be righteousness for you.'
If he does not acquire the collateral,
from where is the righteousness?
From here we learn that a creditor acquires the collateral.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the teaching of רבי יצחק that step 1 said the תנאים disagree about.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A בעל חוב acquires the משכון he holds, learned from 'ולך תהיה צדקה'.

steps.title: תנא קמא: the rule applies only between two Jews
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא limits רבי יצחק's rule to a ישראל taking a משכון from another ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: The first תנא holds: this rule applies only to a Jew taking collateral from a Jew, because only there does the פסוק 'it shall be righteousness for you' apply. But a Jew taking collateral from a גוי does not acquire it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the תנא קמא's view. The rule that a lender owns the משכון applies only between two Jews.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The source of the rule is a פסוק about returning a pledge to a fellow ישראל. So the תנא קמא does not extend it to a pledge taken from a גוי. The חמץ therefore stays the גוי's, and the ישראל does not transgress on פסח.

keyTerms.meaning: The first (unnamed) opinion in a ברייתא or משנה.

phrases.english: The first Tanna holds:
This applies only to a Jew taking collateral from a Jew,
about whom I can read 'and it shall be righteousness for you,'
but a Jew taking collateral from a gentile
does not acquire it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies רבי יצחק's rule to the תנא קמא in a limited way.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A ישראל does not acquire a משכון from a גוי, so he does not transgress with the גוי's חמץ.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: all the more so from a gentile
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר uses a קל וחומר to extend the rule to a ישראל taking a משכון from a גוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר holds there is a קל וחומר: if a Jew acquires collateral from a fellow Jew, then surely he acquires it from a גוי!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רבי מאיר's view. He reasons that if the rule applies between Jews, it applies even more to collateral taken from a גוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה is more protective of a fellow ישראל's property than of a גוי's. So if a lender owns a ישראל's pledge, he certainly owns a גוי's pledge. That is why רבי מאיר says the ישראל owns the חמץ on פסח and transgresses.

keyTerms.meaning: A logical argument from a lighter case to a stronger one.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Meir holds there is an a fortiori argument:
If a Jew acquires collateral from a Jew,
a Jew from a gentile, all the more so!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view to the תנא קמא in step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A ישראל acquires a משכון from a גוי, so he transgresses with the חמץ held as collateral.
steps.whatToRemember: Both sides accept רבי יצחק's rule. The תנא קמא limits it to a ישראל lending to a ישראל, while רבי מאיר extends it by a קל וחומר to a ישראל lending to a גוי.

steps.title: Everyone agrees: a gentile never acquires collateral from a Jew
steps.stepSummary: When a גוי lends to a ישראל against the ישראל's חמץ, all agree that the ישראל transgresses, because a גוי does not acquire a משכון.
steps.simpleTranslation: But when a גוי lends money to a ישראל and takes the ישראל's חמץ as collateral, everyone agrees that after פסח the ישראל has transgressed. In that case, a גוי certainly does not acquire collateral from a ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets a limit that both sides agree on. רבי יצחק's ownership rule never works for a גוי lender.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק and the קל וחומר are both about a ישראל lender. A גוי lender is not included at all. So the חמץ stays the ישראל's on פסח, and he transgresses בל יראה.

keyTerms.meaning: Transgresses (here, the prohibition of owning חמץ on פסח).

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל גּוֹי שֶׁהִלְוָה אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל עַל חֲמֵצוֹ —
phrases.english: But a gentile who lent money to a Jew against his leavened bread,
after Passover, all agree that he transgresses.

phrases.aramaic: הָתָם וַדַּאי גּוֹי מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל לָא קָנֵי.
phrases.english: There, a gentile certainly does not acquire collateral from a Jew.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל גּוֹי שֶׁהִלְוָה אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל עַל חֲמֵצוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets the outer limit of the argument from steps 3 and 4. In the reverse case, nobody disagrees.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גוי lender does not acquire a ישראל's משכון. The חמץ stays the ישראל's, and he transgresses.
steps.whyThisMatters: This all-agree rule sets up the question in the next step from the משנה.

steps.title: Challenge from the משנה: why is the חמץ permitted?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה permits benefit from a ישראל's חמץ held by a גוי lender. That seems to contradict the rule that a גוי never acquires a משכון.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: if a גוי lent money to a ישראל against his חמץ, after פסח the חמץ is permitted for benefit. Even if the חמץ was placed with the גוי, didn't you just say that a גוי does not acquire collateral from a ישראל?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the rule from step 5 using the משנה. If the גוי never owned the חמץ, it was the ישראל's on פסח and should be forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חמץ that a ישראל owned over פסח is forbidden even for benefit. The משנה's permission seems to show that the גוי owned it. But step 5 said a גוי cannot acquire a משכון, so the two seem to clash.
steps.confusionAlert: The direction of the deposit has flipped. In step 1, the גוי borrower placed his חמץ with the ישראל lender. Here, the ישראל borrower placed his חמץ with the גוי lender.

phrases.english: We learned in the Mishnah:
A gentile who lent money to a Jew against his leavened bread,
after Passover it is permitted to derive benefit from it.
Even granted that he deposited it with him (the gentile),

phrases.aramaic: הָא אָמְרַתְּ גּוֹי מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל לָא קָנֵי?
phrases.english: didn't you say that a gentile does not acquire collateral from a Jew?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the all-agree rule in step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that a גוי does not acquire a משכון from a ישראל (step 5).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה permits the חמץ after פסח, which means the גוי owned it. But by step 5 he could not own it, so it should be forbidden.

steps.title: It depends on whether the gentile said 'from now'
steps.stepSummary: The משנה's case is where the גוי stipulated 'מעכשיו'. The forbidding case is where he did not.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. The משנה is talking about a case where the גוי told the ישראל, 'from now.' The rule that he transgresses is about a case where the גוי did not say 'from now.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the challenge by splitting it into two cases, depending on whether the deal included the condition 'מעכשיו'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With 'מעכשיו', if the ישראל fails to repay, the גוי owns the חמץ backwards from the time of the loan, before פסח. That is a regular acquisition, not רבי יצחק's משכון rule, so the חמץ was never the ישראל's on פסח and is permitted. Without 'מעכשיו', the גוי only takes it after פסח, so the ישראל owned it during פסח and it is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult (introduces an answer).
From now, meaning ownership takes effect backwards from the time of the deal.
This case... that case (splitting into two cases).

steps.whatToRemember: A גוי lender never owns a משכון just by holding it. He can still own the חמץ through a 'מעכשיו' condition, which makes him the owner from before פסח. Then the חמץ is permitted after פסח.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
this case is where he said to him 'from now,'
and that case is where he did not say to him 'from now.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא in step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splits the cases (הא בכך הא בכך) based on a 'מעכשיו' condition.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's permission contradicts the rule that a גוי cannot acquire a ישראל's משכון.
steps.terutzMaskana: With 'מעכשיו', the גוי owns the חמץ backwards from before פסח, so it is permitted. Without it, the חמץ stayed the ישראל's and is forbidden.

steps.title: Bringing a source that 'from now' makes a difference
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where we see that saying 'מעכשיו' changes the law, and quotes a ברייתא about a גוי who leaves bread as collateral with a ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where do you know that there is a difference between when he said 'from now' and when he did not say 'from now'? As it was taught in a ברייתא: If a גוי left oven-baked bread as collateral with a ישראל, the ישראל does not transgress. But if the גוי said to him 'it is yours,' the ישראל does transgress.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is backing up its last answer (step 7) by bringing a ברייתא. This step sets up the evidence, and the next step will draw the conclusion from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 7 the גמרא answered that a 'מעכשיו' stipulation changes who owns the משכון. Now it brings a ברייתא with two cases that differ only in whether the borrower said 'הגעתיך' ('it has reached you,' meaning it is yours from now). In the plain case the ישראל holding the bread does not transgress בל יראה. When 'הגעתיך' was said, he does transgress.

keyTerms.meaning: And from where do you say this? (asks for a source)
Bread baked in a large oven
'It has reached you' — it is yours (from now)

steps.confusionAlert: Notice the roles are flipped from step 7. There the גוי was the lender. Here the גוי is the borrower who leaves bread with the ישראל lender. The point being proven is the same: 'מעכשיו' changes the result.

phrases.english: And from where do you say
that there is a difference between where he said 'from now'
phrases.notes: Refers to the distinction made in step 7.

phrases.english: and where he did not say 'from now'?
As it was taught in a ברייתא:

phrases.aramaic: גּוֹי שֶׁהִרְהִין פַּת פּוּרְנִי אֵצֶל יִשְׂרָאֵל —
phrases.english: A gentile who left oven-baked bread as collateral with a Jew —
he (the Jew) does not transgress,
but if he said to him 'it is yours' — he transgresses.
phrases.notes: 'הגעתיך' works like 'מעכשיו': the bread belongs to the lender starting now.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to support the תירוץ of step 7.
steps.raayaObject: The distinction between a משכון given with 'מעכשיו' and one given without it.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about a גוי leaving פת פורני as collateral with a ישראל, with and without 'הגעתיך'.

steps.title: Drawing the conclusion from the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: Only the 'from now' wording separates the two halves of the ברייתא, so that wording must be what matters. The גמרא accepts this.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between the first part and the last part? Must we not learn from this that there is a difference between when he said 'from now' and when he did not say 'from now'? Yes, learn from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the only difference between the two cases is the 'it is yours' wording. It concludes that this wording is what makes the difference.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof works by elimination. The case is the same in both halves (same bread, same loan), and only the stipulation changes, yet the ruling changes. So the stipulation 'מעכשיו' must be what changes who owns the collateral. This confirms step 7's answer.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different about the first clause?

steps.whatToRemember: A 'מעכשיו' / 'הגעתיך' condition makes the lender the owner of the משכון. This proves the distinction used in step 7 to answer the קשיא. Without such a condition, a גוי's משכון held by a ישראל stays the גוי's according to the תנא קמא. Under רבי מאיר, the ישראל owns it anyway through רבי יצחק's rule.

phrases.english: What is different in the first clause
and what is different in the latter clause?
Rather, must one not learn from it:
that it is different where he said to him 'from now'
from where he did not say to him 'from now'?
Indeed, learn from it.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי שְׁנָא רֵישָׁא וּמַאי שְׁנָא סֵיפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the proof begun in step 8 and confirms it.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Saying 'מעכשיו' changes the ownership of a משכון, which confirms the answer of step 7.

steps.title: חמץ found in a Jewish-owned store after פסח
steps.stepSummary: If the store and its stock belong to a ישראל, חמץ found there after פסח is forbidden even for benefit, even though גוי workers come in.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: A store that belongs to a ישראל, with stock that belongs to a ישראל, and גוי workers come in there — חמץ found there after פסח is forbidden for benefit, and certainly it is forbidden to eat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching (a תוספתא) about how to decide who owned חמץ found after פסח. This is the first of two matching cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We assume the חמץ belongs to the owner of the store and its contents, here a ישראל. We do not say it might have been left by the גוי workers. A ישראל's חמץ that stayed in his possession over פסח (חמץ שעבר עליו הפסח) is forbidden even for benefit.

keyTerms.meaning: Forbidden to get any benefit from

phrases.english: The Sages taught:

phrases.aramaic: חֲנוּת שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל וּמְלַאי שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל,
phrases.english: A Jew's store with a Jew's merchandise,
and gentile workers enter there —
leavened bread found there after Passover
is forbidden for benefit,
and needless to say, for eating.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new ברייתא that turns to a related question about who owns חמץ.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חמץ found after פסח in a ישראל's store with a ישראל's stock is presumed to be his and is forbidden for benefit.

steps.title: חמץ found in a gentile-owned store after פסח
steps.stepSummary: If the store and its stock belong to a גוי, חמץ found there after פסח is permitted even to eat, even though ישראל workers come and go.
steps.simpleTranslation: A store that belongs to a גוי, with stock that belongs to a גוי, and ישראל workers come in and go out — חמץ found there after פסח is permitted to eat, and certainly permitted for benefit.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the mirror case of the same ברייתא. The store and its stock now belong to a גוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Again, the חמץ is presumed to belong to whoever owns the store and its contents, here the גוי. We do not worry that a ישראל worker left it. A גוי's חמץ over פסח is not forbidden to a ישראל, so it may even be eaten.
steps.whatToRemember: חמץ found after פסח follows the owner of the store and its stock, not the workers who pass through.

phrases.aramaic: חֲנוּת שֶׁל גּוֹי וּמְלַאי שֶׁל גּוֹי
phrases.english: A gentile's store with a gentile's merchandise
and Jewish workers enter and exit there —
leavened bread found there after Passover
is permitted for eating,
and needless to say, for benefit.

steps.triggerLanguage: חֲנוּת שֶׁל גּוֹי וּמְלַאי שֶׁל גּוֹי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The mirror case of step 10 in the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חמץ found after פסח in a גוי's store with a גוי's stock is presumed to be the גוי's and is permitted even to eat.

steps.title: חמץ buried under a collapse counts as destroyed
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: חמץ covered by a pile of rubble is treated as if it was already destroyed.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: חמץ that a collapse of rubble fell on is considered as if it was destroyed.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It says you do not need to dig out חמץ that is buried under fallen rubble.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a person must destroy (בער) his חמץ. Here the חמץ is treated as already destroyed, so there is no need to dig it up and burn it.

keyTerms.meaning: A collapse / pile of fallen rubble
As if destroyed (as if ביעור was done)

phrases.english: MISHNA:
Leavened bread on which a collapse of rubble fell
is considered as though destroyed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חמץ buried under a מפולת counts as destroyed.

steps.title: How deep the rubble must be: beyond a dog's reach
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says the חמץ counts as destroyed only if it is buried so deep that a dog cannot dig for it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: Any חמץ that a dog cannot search after.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל adds a measure to the משנה's rule: the חמץ must be covered deeply enough that a dog could not dig it out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first part of the משנה did not say how much rubble is needed. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל sets the standard: out of a dog's reach. If a dog could still find it, it is not considered destroyed.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא, נשיא of the סנהדרין

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל שֶׁאֵין הַכֶּלֶב יָכוֹל לְחַפֵּשׂ אַחֲרָיו.
phrases.english: Any that a dog cannot search after.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets the depth needed for the משנה's rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Buried חמץ counts as destroyed only when a dog cannot dig for it.

steps.title: רב חסדא: one must still nullify it in his heart
steps.stepSummary: Even though buried חמץ counts as destroyed, רב חסדא says the owner must still do ביטול in his heart.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רב חסדא said: And he must nullify it in his heart.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with רב חסדא adding a condition to the משנה: the owner must still declare the buried חמץ ownerless and worthless in his mind.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rubble might be cleared away during פסח, and then the owner would own visible חמץ and transgress בל יראה. Doing ביטול now protects him, because then the חמץ is no longer his.

keyTerms.meaning: That he nullify it in his heart (ביטול)

steps.confusionAlert: 'כמבוער' does not mean nothing more is needed. According to רב חסדא the person still has to do ביטול.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basis for the practical rule that ביטול is needed even for חמץ one cannot reach.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Rav Ḥisda said:
And he must nullify it in his heart.
phrases.notes: In case the rubble is removed during פסח.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: וְצָרִיךְ שֶׁיְּבַטֵּל בְּלִבּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a condition to the משנה's ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Buried חמץ still requires ביטול בלב.

steps.title: A dog digs three טפחים deep
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא gives the exact measure: a dog digs three טפחים, so חמץ covered by three טפחים of rubble is out of its reach.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: How far does a dog dig? Three טפחים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that puts a number on רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's measure from the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Out of a dog's reach' is now defined: a dog digs three טפחים deep. So חמץ covered by three טפחים or more of rubble is considered destroyed.
steps.whatToRemember: Buried חמץ counts as destroyed if it is under three טפחים of rubble, and (רב חסדא) one must still do ביטול.

phrases.english: It was taught:
How much is a dog's search —
three handbreadths.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the number for the measure in step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A dog digs three טפחים, so חמץ buried deeper than that is out of its reach.

steps.title: Does buried money also need three טפחים?
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרב יוסף asks רב אשי whether שמואל's rule about burying money also needs a depth of three טפחים, like buried חמץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא son of רב יוסף said to רב אשי: שמואל said that money is only properly guarded when it is buried in the ground. Does it need to be buried three טפחים deep, or not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא just learned that buried חמץ must be more than three טפחים deep. Now someone asks whether the same depth applies to a different burial rule, about guarding money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל taught that a שומר who wants to guard money properly must bury it in the ground. Since we just learned a measurement for burying חמץ, the question is whether that measurement carries over to money. This is a clarifying question, not an attack.

keyTerms.meaning: Money (here, money given to someone to watch)
Proper guarding. A שומר who guards properly is not liable if the money is lost.

steps.confusionAlert: This is not about חמץ anymore. It is a side question about a שומר guarding money. The only link is the depth of burial.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יוֹסֵף לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Acha son of Rav Yosef said to Rav Ashi:
That which Shmuel said,
Money has no proper guarding
except in the ground,

phrases.aramaic: מִי בָּעֵינַן שְׁלֹשָׁה טְפָחִים אוֹ לָא?
phrases.english: do we require three handbreadths, or not?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי בָּעֵינַן שְׁלֹשָׁה טְפָחִים אוֹ לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the three-טפחים measure from Step 15 to a new case, money buried by a שומר.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether money must be buried three טפחים deep to count as properly guarded.

steps.title: חמץ is hidden from smell, money is hidden from sight
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that חמץ needs three טפחים because of its smell, while money only needs to be hidden from view, so three טפחים are not required.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Here, with חמץ, we need three טפחים because of the smell. There, with money, the point is to hide it from the eye, so it does not need three.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי explains that the two cases have different reasons, so they need different depths.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With חמץ, the worry is that a dog will smell it and dig it up, so it must be deeper than a dog digs. With money, there is no smell, and the worry is only that a person will see it. A shallower burial is enough to keep it out of sight.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a measurement depends on the reason behind the rule. Change the reason, and the measurement can change too.

phrases.english: He said to him:
Here, because of the smell,
we require three handbreadths.
There, it is in order to be hidden from the eye,
and it does not require three.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא מִשּׁוּם רֵיחָא בָּעֵינַן שְׁלֹשָׁה טְפָחִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Money does not need three טפחים, because the burial is to hide it from sight, not from a dog's sense of smell.

steps.title: So how deep must money be buried?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what depth is enough for money, since it does not need three טפחים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how much?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that we know money does not need three טפחים, the גמרא asks for the actual depth. This short question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying "less than three" is not a clear rule. The גמרא wants an exact minimum so a שומר knows when he has guarded properly.

phrases.english: And how much?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on Step 17, asking for the exact smaller depth.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The minimum depth for burying money.

steps.title: One טפח is enough for money
steps.stepSummary: רפרם בר פפא from סיכרא says that one טפח is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: רפרם בר פפא from סיכרא said: one טפח.
steps.whatsHappening: רפרם בר פפא gives the exact depth: money buried one טפח deep counts as properly guarded.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One טפח is enough to hide the money from people's eyes. This closes the side discussion about burial depth.
steps.whatToRemember: Buried חמץ must be covered by three טפחים, beyond a dog's search, because of its smell. Buried money needs only one טפח, because it only has to be hidden from sight.

phrases.english: Rafram bar Pappa from Sikhra said:
One handbreadth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 18's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Money must be buried one טפח deep.

steps.title: New משנה: eating תרומה of חמץ on פסח
steps.stepSummary: Someone who eats תרומה of חמץ on פסח by accident pays the value plus a fifth. If he did it on purpose, he pays nothing, not even its value as firewood.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: One who eats תרומה of חמץ on פסח: if by accident, he pays the principal and an added fifth. If on purpose, he is exempt from payment and from paying its value as firewood.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It discusses a person who eats a כהן's תרומה that is חמץ, during פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, someone who eats תרומה by accident pays the כהן its value plus a fifth (קרן וחומש). This משנה says the rule still applies even though חמץ on פסח has no market value. If he eats it on purpose, he deserves כרת, so he is exempt from payment. He also does not pay its "firewood value" (the value of טמאה תרומה, which is normally used as fuel), because benefit from חמץ on פסח is forbidden, so even that value does not exist.

keyTerms.meaning: The portion of produce given to a כהן
The principal (the value) plus an added fifth

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the person who sinned on purpose gets off easier. He is exempt from paying only because he faces a much harsher punishment, כרת.

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
One who eats teruma of leavened bread on Passover,
if unwittingly, pays the principal and a fifth;
if intentionally, he is exempt from payment
and from its value as firewood.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה with a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Eating תרומה of חמץ on פסח by accident requires paying קרן וחומש. Doing it on purpose brings no payment at all, not even firewood value.

steps.title: The גמרא quotes a related משנה from מסכת תרומות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins by quoting a משנה elsewhere: one who eats תרומה by accident pays the principal and a fifth, whether he ate it or drank it.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: We learned there: One who eats תרומה by accident pays the principal and a fifth, both one who eats and one who drinks.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens its discussion of our משנה by quoting the basic rule from מסכת תרומות. It is setting up a comparison that will be developed next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The base rule is that accidentally eating תרומה requires קרן וחומש, and drinking counts the same as eating. The גמרא brings this source to help explain our משנה's ruling about חמץ.

keyTerms.meaning: We learned in a משנה elsewhere

phrases.english: GEMARA: We learned there:
One who eats teruma unwittingly
pays the principal and a fifth,
both one who eats and one who drinks

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the גמרא on the משנה of Step 20 by bringing a parallel source.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Accidentally eating or drinking תרומה requires paying קרן וחומש.
